# Priscilla Grant

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c34 P4](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0004)</sub>
- **Role:** Student, and later a teacher  <sub>[v1 c34 P4](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0004), [v2 c1 P57](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0057)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Pris  <sub>[v2 c4 P5](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0005)</sub>; The 'dream girl'  <sub>[v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004)</sub>

## Appearance

Priscilla is a tall, pale, and spiritual-looking maiden with lovely hair. She has a high-bred appearance and looks as if she knows a thing or two about dreams. Her aunt once remarked that she possessed 'ethereal, golden beauty.'

_Sources: [v1 c34 P12](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0012), [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v2 c4 P6](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0006), [v2 c4 P20](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0020)_

## Personality

Despite her pale, spiritual appearance, Priscilla is full to the brim of mischief, pranks, and fun. She has a clever, humorous mind and enjoys gay, good-natured banter, though she can be deeply reflective about life and literature. She possesses a very unselfish and appreciative nature, readily acknowledging the talents and gifts of her friends.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v1 c37 P23](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0023), [v2 c4 P12](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0012), [v2 c6 P5](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0005)_

## Traits

- Full of mischief, pranks, and fun  <sub>[v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004)</sub>
- Unselfish and appreciative
- Loves nature and literature  <sub>[v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v1 c37 P23](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0023)</sub>

## Abilities

- Skilled in Classics and story-writing  <sub>[v1 c26 P20](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0020), [v1 c35 P5](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0005)</sub>

## Goals

- To earn her B.A. degree at Redmond College and pursue a career in teaching  <sub>[v1 c30 P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v1 c34 P11](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0011)</sub>

## History

Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley, where she distinguished herself as an ambitious and clever student. After graduating, she taught school in Carmody for a time before deciding to further her education. She entered Redmond College in Kingsport, taking up the Second Year work alongside Anne. At Redmond, Priscilla, Anne, and Philippa Gordon became close friends and lived together at 'Patty's Place,' a quaint cottage on Spofford Avenue, under the care of Aunt Jamesina. During her college years, she excelled in Classics and participated actively in campus social life and the Story Club. After completing her Sophomore year, she accepted a teaching position at her home school.

_Sources: [v1 c34 P11](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0011), [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v1 c35 P5](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0005), [v2 c1 P57](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0057), [v2 c6 P5](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0005), [v2 c9 P13](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0013), [v2 c10 P32](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0032), [v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060)_

## Background by volume

- Attended Queen's Academy with Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe  <sub>[v1 c34 P11](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0011)</sub>
- Taught school in Carmody before going to Redmond College  <sub>[v2 c1 P57](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0057), [v2 c4 P5](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0005)</sub>
- Is the niece of the famous author Charlotte E. Morgan  <sub>[v2 c6 P5](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0005)</sub>

> It’s a lot nicer than going round by the road; that is so dusty and hot.  <sub>[v1 c15 P1](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0001)</sub>

> If a kiss could be seen I think it would look like a violet.  <sub>[v2 c13 P11](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0011)</sub>

> There is so much in the world for us all if we only have the eyes to see it, and the heart to love it, and the hand to gather it to ourselves—so much in men and women, so much in art and literature, so much everywhere in which to delight, and for which to be thankful.  <sub>[v1 c37 P23](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0023)</sub>

> I’m afraid we can’t afford quite so much. You see, we are only college girls and we are poor.  <sub>[v2 c10 P15](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0015)</sub>
